'''Mouhamed Saer Sene''' (born May 12, 1986) is a Senegalese former professional [[basketball]] player. He has a 7 ft 8½ in (2.35 m) wingspan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Saer-Sene-246/|title=Saer Sene, Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook|work=DraftExpress.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Born and raised in [[Thiès|Thiès, Senegal]], Sene originally went to a private school to become a mechanic, but his father pushed him toward basketball.<ref name=prospect>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2006/profiles/SaerSene.html|title=Prospect Profile: Saer Sene|work=NBA.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> In 2003, he joined the SEED Academy, a program designed to send Senegalese youths to the United States to play college basketball.<ref>{{cite web|last=Chan|first=Lorne|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/planting-seeds-boris|title=Planting Seeds With Boris|work=NBA.com|date=May 13, 2015|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref>

Between 2004 and 2005, Sene attended two Reebok Eurocamps in [[Treviso|Treviso, Italy]], participated in the Berlin Adidas Camp, played exhibition games against NCAA teams with the Interhoop African All-Stars touring team, and played in Belgium for the [[Spirou Charleroi|Spirou Basket]] junior squad.<ref name="prospect" />

==Professional career==

===Verviers-Pepinster (2005–2006)===
Sene's first professional season came in 2005–06, when he joined [[VOO Wolves Verviers-Pepinster]] of the [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Belgian League]]. He appeared in 25 games for Verviers-Pepinster, averaging 4.0 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 12.3 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gamecent/p/leagueid/BEL/ot/1/pid/6034463/season/2006/tid/6010682/playerview.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304013538/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gamecent/p/leagueid/BEL/ot/1/pid/6034463/season/2006/tid/6010682/playerview.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2016|title=Saer SENE | Season 2005/2006|work=FIBA.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref>

===NBA (2006–2009)===

====2006–07 season====
On June 28, 2006, Sene was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] with the 10th overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Diaz|first=John|url=http://spursonsixth.com/2015/03/austin-spurs-acquire-mouhamed-saer-sene/|title=Austin Spurs Acquire Mouhamed Saer Sene|work=spursonsixth.com|date=March 24, 2015|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He played sparingly for the SuperSonics over the first two months of the 2006–07 season, managing to appear in just 16 games by early January. On January 10, 2007, he was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/sonics-assign-center-mouhamed-sene-to-idaho-stampede/n-3414158|title=Sonics assign center Mouhamed Sene to Idaho Stampede|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 10, 2007|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> a stint which lasted until January 26. In his first game back for the SuperSonics on January 28, he scored a season-high 10 points in 12 minutes off the bench against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He was later reassigned to Idaho on February 3 and spent the majority of the month of February in the D-League. He finished his rookie season playing in nine games over March and April, totalling 28 games for the SuperSonics in 2006–07.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/senesa01/gamelog/2007/|title=Mouhamed Sene 2006-07 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref>

====2007–08 season====
Sene returned to the SuperSonics for the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]] but managed just 13 games for the entire season. He spent the majority of his time in the D-League playing for the Idaho Stampede, earning [[NBA Development League Defensive Player of the Year Award|D-League Defensive Player of the Year]] honors alongside [[Stéphane Lasme]] at season's end.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/defensive_players_080410.html|title=Stephane Lasme and Mouhamed Sene Named Co-Defensive Players of the Year|work=NBA.com|date=April 10, 2008|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> In 28 games for Idaho in 2007–08, Sene averaged 12.1 points, 8.9 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 27.5 minutes per game.

====2008–09 season====
With the SuperSonics' relocation to Oklahoma City in 2008, Sene continued on with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in 2008–09. Due to off-season knee surgery, Sene missed the start of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rotowire.com/basketball/player.htm?id=2724|title=Mouhamed Sene Fantasy Stats|work=RotoWire.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He played in five games for the Thunder during November 2008, but following this, he did not play in another game for the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/senesa01/gamelog/2009/|title=Mouhamed Sene 2008-09 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> On February 19, 2009, Sene was waived by the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/aquirethabo_090219.html |title=Thunder Acquires Thabo Sefolosha |work=NBA.com |date=February 19, 2009 |accessdate=March 9, 2013}}</ref>

On March 11, 2009, Sene was acquired by the [[New Mexico Thunderbirds|Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] of the NBA D-League. He played in 10 games for the Thunderbirds before being called up to the NBA by the [[New York Knicks]], signing a rest-of-season contract with the team on April 9.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4122|title=Knicks sign Mouhamed Sene|work=InsideHoops.com|date=April 9, 2009|accessdate=March 9, 2013}}</ref> He managed just one game for the Knicks over the final week of the regular season, and on July 31, he was waived by the team.{{cn|date=April 2023}}

===France (2009–2011)===
On September 26, 2009, Sene signed with [[Hyères-Toulon Var Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/78952/hyeres-toulon-goes-big-with-sene.html|title=Hyeres-Toulon goes big with Sene|work=Sportando.com|date=September 26, 2009|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in 29 games for Hyères-Toulon in 2009–10, averaging 12.4 points, a league-best 11.4 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game.

On June 12, 2010, Sene signed a two-year deal with [[Spirou Charleroi|Spirou Basket]], the team he launched his career with in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/72891/charleroi-tabs-mouhamed-saer-sene-at-center|title=Charleroi tabs Mouhamed Saer Sene at center|work=Euroleague.net|date=June 12, 2010|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He later left the club before appearing in a game for them, and on November 21, 2010, he signed with French club [[BCM Gravelines|BCM Gravelines Dunkerque]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Sene-signe-a-gravelines/158608|title=Sene signe à Gravelines|work=lequipe.fr|date=November 21, 2010|accessdate=February 26, 2016|language=French}}</ref> In 25 league games for Gravelines in 2010–11, he averaged 10.4 points, 7.4 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game.

===Spain (2011–2013)===
On August 16, 2011, Sene signed a two-year deal with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/88081/fuenlabrada-announces-saer-sene.html|title=Fuenlabrada announces Saer Sene|work=Sportando.com|date=August 16, 2011|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He sustained an injury in January 2012, which forced him to sit out the remainder of the season. He appeared in 15 league games for Fuenlabrada in 2011–12, averaging 6.3 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.7 blocks per game.

Sene returned to Fuenlabrada in 2012–13, playing in 30 games and averaging 5.4 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game.

===Second stint in France (2013)===
On July 30, 2013, Sene signed a two-year deal with French club [[Olympique Antibes|Sharks Antibes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Accueil/100003/Article/18644/Mouhamed-Saer-Sene-a-Antibes|title=Mouhamed Saer Sene in Antibes|work=LNB.fr|date=July 30, 2013|accessdate=February 26, 2016|language=French}}</ref> A knee injury suffered in October forced Sene to miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/107338/antibes-big-man-saer-sene-done-for-the-season.html|title=Antibes big man Saer Sene done for the season?|work=Sportando.com|date=October 25, 2013|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in just three games for Antibes, averaging 8.7 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals per game.

===Austin Spurs (2015–2016)===
On March 18, 2015, Sene was acquired by the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-mouhamed-saer-sene/|title=AUSTIN SPURS ACQUIRE MOUHAMED SAER SENE|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2015|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> In 13 games (seven regular season, six playoff) for the Spurs in 2014–15, he averaged 20.3 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.6 blocks per game.

On February 26, 2016, Sene was reacquired by Austin.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-mouhamed-sene/|title=Austin Spurs Acquire Mouhamed Sene|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2016|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> On March 22, he was waived by the Spurs. He made just one appearance for the team, recording two points and three rebounds in 16 minutes on March 6 against the Idaho Stampede.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-waive-mouhamed-sene/|title=Austin Spurs Waive Mouhamed Sene|work=NBA.com|date=March 22, 2016|accessdate=March 22, 2016}}</ref>

==National team career==
Sene first played for the [[Senegal national basketball team]] during the [[AfroBasket 2013|2013 AfroBasket]]. The following year, he missed out on the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] due to the knee injury sustained while playing for [[Olympique Antibes|Sharks Antibes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/news/SEN-Sarr--I-think-made-the-right-choices-|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720160800/http://www.fiba.com/basketballworldcup/2014/news/SEN-Sarr--I-think-made-the-right-choices-|url-status=live|archive-date=July 20, 2014|title=SEN – Sarr: "I think I made the right choices"|work=FIBA.com|date=July 17, 2014|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref> He returned to the national team for the [[AfroBasket 2015|2015 AfroBasket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/q/Saer%20Sene/pid//_//players.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903211857/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/q/Saer%20Sene/pid//_//players.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 3, 2014|title=Saer Sene – FIBA Archive|work=FIBA.com|accessdate=February 26, 2016}}</ref>
